newsitem.title: UK: Sema Group yr profits soar, upbeat on '97.
newsitem.headline: Sema Group yr profits soar, upbeat on '97.

text.p: Sema Group Plc, the UK information technology services company, reported a 35 percent hike in year pretax profits to 50 million stg on Tuesday and said it expected that success to continue into 1997.

The group said its strategy of focusing on telecoms, industry and finance paid off with rapid rises in turnover. The group saw organic sales growth of 20 percent in all, with turnover at 927 million stg versus 677 million.

The total dividend payout was up to six pence per share from five pence the previous year. Pierre Bonelli, group chief executive, said recent business systems acquisitions -- Syntax, Telis and BR Business Systems -- placed the group for continued growth.
That last two are seen adding 170 million stg to group turnover in 1997 and the rail business is seen benefiting from the privatisation of the UK rail network, now complete.
Sema said its growth plans were being achieved more rapidly than expected, with the order book as well as turnover showing record increases.
